75
RAJYA  SABHA
————
List of Questions for ORAL  ANSWERS
to be asked at a sitting of the Rajya Sabha to be held on
Friday, the December 9, 2005/Agrahayana 18, 1927 (Saka)
————
(Ministries : Agriculture; Chemicals and Fertilizers; Consumer Affairs, Food
and Public Distribution; Environment and Forests; Food Processing
Industries; Health and Family Welfare; Railways; Steel)
Total number of questions — 20
Revival of Gorakhpur and Sindri
fertilizer units
*241. SHRI RAJEEV SHUKLA: Will
the Minister of CHEMICALS AND
FERTILIZERS be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that Government
are considering the revival of the Gorakhpur
and Sindri units of the Fertilizer
Corporation of India, by setting up gas-
based brownfield fertilizer plants at the
existing sites;
(b) if so, the details of the proposal;
(c) whether it is also a fact that GAIL
has agreed to supply gas to the units by
2010; and
(d) by when the units are scheduled to
be operational?
Complaints against slaughter houses
causing environmental pollution
†*242. DR. CHHATTRAPAL SINGH
LODHA: Will the Minister of
ENVIRONMENT AND FORESTS be
pleased to state:
(a) the number of complaints received
by the Central Pollution Control Board and
the State Pollution Control Boards/
Committees during the last three years
regarding environmental pollution caused
by slaughter houses;
(b) the names of complainants and the
details of their complaints alongwith the
names of those against whom each
complaint has been made;
(c) the action taken by the Central
Pollution Control Board and the State
Pollution Control Boards/Committees on
such complaints; and
(d) whether complainants have also
been apprised of the outcome of inquiry?
Antyodaya Anna Yojana in Andhra
Pradesh
*243. SHRI NANDI YELLAIAH: Will
the Minister of CONSUMER AFFAIRS,
FOOD AND PUBLIC DISTRIBUTION
be pleased to state:
(a) whether the Society for Elimination
of Rural Poverty has estimated that in
Andhra Pradesh, 23,84,535 families are at
the risk of hunger;
(b) whether at present 12,33,600
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.

76
families are covered under the Antyodaya
Anna Yojana scheme in the State;
(c) if so, the details thereof;
(d) the details of the scheme and
guidelines for its implementation;
(e) whether 13,49,990 families are yet
to be covered under this scheme;
(f) if so, the details thereof; and
(g) whether Government would take
immediate steps to cover all these families,
including all the left-over families under the
scheme?
CBI raids in hospitals
*244. SHRI DATTA MEGHE: Will the
Minister of HEALTH AND FAMILY
WELFARE be pleased to state:
(a) whether the Central Bureau of
Investigation (CBI) has conducted raids on
certain hospitals in Delhi and other cities;
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) the reasons for conducting raids on
these hospitals;
(d) the incriminating documents seized
from these concerned hospitals;
(e) whether any arrests have, so far,
been made;
(f) if so, the details thereof; and
(g) the departmental action so far taken
or proposed to be taken against the
concerned officers of these hospitals?
Linking of Gurgaon/Rewari/Alwar
with Punjab
*245. SHRI DHARAM PAL
SABHARWAL: Will the Minister of
RAILWAYS be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government have received
any representations to link Gurgaon/
Rewari/Alwar with Punjab by extending/
diverting some of the trains which terminate
at Delhi/New Delhi;
(b) if so, by when; and
(c) if not, the reasons therefor?
Agriculture as knowledge-based
industry
*246. SHRIMATI JAMANA DEVI
BARUPAL:
DR. T. SUBBARAMI
REDDY:
Will the Minister of AGRICUL TURE
be pleased to state:
(a) whether agriculture is becoming a
'knowledge-based' industry globally and in
India if remains of subsistance level,
although over 66 per cent of population
depends on agriculture;
(b) if so, whether experts have urged
India to move forward and be globally
relevant like information technology;
(c) whether India is also a major exporter
of several agricultural commodities and has
earned top position in the production of
milk, wheat, fruits and vegetables;
(d) whether Government have
considered setting up more open
universities for agriculture; and
(e) if so, the other steps Government
propose to take in this regard?
M.S. Swaminathan Committee
*247. DR. CHANDAN MITRA: Will
the Minister of ENVIRONMENT AND
FORESTS be pleased to state:
(a) whether a Committee headed by the
scientist Prof. M.S. Swaminathan has been
set up to recommend steps to be taken
along the Indian coastline in view of the
Tsunami disaster last year;

77
(b) whether it is proposed to draw a
vulnerability line along the coast and amend
the Coastal Regulation Zone (CRZ) along
this proposed line;
(c) whether it is proposed that new
construction is to be allowed only beyond
1500 mts. from the coast; and
(d) whether Government have taken
into account its impact on beach tourism
and hotel locations if construction is banned
upto one and a half kms. from the shore?

Central Tobacco Research Institute
1802. SHRI V. HANUMANTHA
RAO: Will the Minister of
AGRICULTURE be pleased to state:
(a) the role of the Central Tobacco
Research Institute;
(b) whether it is a fact that very little
positive, constructive and useful research
has come out of the CTRI in the last three
years;
(c) the steps proposed to energise this
body in the interest of the farmers; and
(d) the details of measures proposed in
this regard?
Venture capital fund
1803. SHRI MOOLCHAND
MEENA:
DR. T. SUBBARAMI
REDDY:
 Will the Minister of AGRICULTURE
be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government have
approved Rs. 48 crores venture capital fund
or agri-sector business;
(b) if so, whether this venture capital is
accepted to provide much needed relief to
farmers for whom one of the biggest hurdles
has been lack of access to easy credit;
(c) whether, in a recent National Sample
Survey Organisation only 15 per cent
farmers said that they had availed of any
loan;
(d) whether, with this venture capital,
they would be able to obtain bigger loans
from banks and its processing will be easier;
and
(e) if so, to what extent this has helped
the farmers and the total funds, so far,
provided to the farmers from this fund?
Loan availability to agriculture sector
†1804. SHRI RAVI SHANKAR
PRASAD:
SHRI RAJ MOHINDER
SINGH MAJITHA:
Will the Minister of AGRICUL TURE
be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that a loan worth
Rs. 7,36,570 crores would be required to
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.

414
be made available by the end of Tenth Five
Year Plan in the agriculture sector of the
country;
(b) if not, the facts thereof;
(c) whether it is also a fact that by the
end of 19th August, 2005, the loan worth
Rs. 1,27,621 crores was required to be
made available in this sector; and
(d) if not, the facts thereof and the loan
availability required to be increased annually
during the remaining years of the Plan in
order to achieve the loan target by the end
of the Plan?
Income of farmers
1805. SHRI ABU ASIM AZMI:
SHRI AMAR SINGH:
Will the Minister of AGRICUL TURE
be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that Indian farmers
are getting today the same price for their
produce which they had been getting
20 years ago as per reports of United Nations
Conference on Trade and Development;
(b) whether it is also a fact that income
of farmers in various parts of the country
has drastically fallen and if so, the details
thereof; and
(c) the remedial steps Government
propose to take in this regard?
Cows and stray cattle
1806. SHRI DHARAM PAL
SABHARWAL: Will the Minister of
AGRICULTURE be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that due to
mechanized farming in Punjab, male calves
in large number have become useless and
are roaming stray in Punjab;
(b) whether the Government of Punjab
has sought permission from Government
to export these stray cattle to the
neighbouring States where bullocks are used
for farming;
(c) whether the permission has been
granted and if not, the reasons therefor;
and
(d) whether the Government of Punjab
have also sought permission from
Government to export cows of cross breed
to the neighbouring States and if so, the
action taken by Government in the matter?
Weather Insurance Scheme
†1807. DR. MURLI MANOHAR
JOSHI:
SHRI RAVI SHANKAR
PRASAD:
Will the Minister of AGRICUL TURE
be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that insurance
scheme is applicable in the country to
compensate the farmers when their crop is
damaged due to bad weather;
(b) if so, the names of the States in the
country wherein insurance scheme is
applicable at present;
(c) the names of the crops for which
this insurance scheme is applicable; and
(d) the number of farmers in the country
benefited by this insurance scheme during
2003-04, 2004-05 and first six months of
2005-06?
Expansion of weather insurance
1808. SHRI DATTA MEGHE: Will the
Minister of AGRICULTURE be pleased
to state:
(a) whether the estimated agriculture
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.

415
losses of nearly Rs. 2000 crores in
Maharashtra and Andhra Pradesh and a
complete eradication of farm income in the
flood affected areas, have brought to light
the need for an expansion of weather
insurance in India;
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) whether at present the insurance
firms do not cover excess rainfall but cover
only the deficient rainfall;
(d) if so, the measures taken by
Government to extend the weather
insurance to cover excess rainfall to benefit
farmers; and
(e) if so, the details thereof and if not,
the reasons therefor?
